title: Personalized Learning Path Planning through Goal-Driven Learner State Modeling
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026 (WWW '26)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of personalized learning path planning (PLPP): how to generate adaptive, goal-aligned sequences of learning activities for individual learners. The authors argue that while large language models can personalize content, they often make short-sighted decisions and do not explicitly model long-term learner development, motivation, or evolving goals. The paper therefore asks how to combine structured learner modeling with reinforcement learning so that a system can plan coherent learning paths that better reflect both cognitive and motivational learner states.

The proposed intervention is Pxplore, a framework that combines a reinforcement-based training paradigm with an LLM-driven educational architecture. The system defines a structured learner state model containing long-term objectives, short-term objectives, implicit motivations, and explicit motivations. It uses an automated reward function to convert progress on these abstract learner-state components into scalar rewards. Training proceeds in two stages: supervised fine-tuning on expert-labeled state-action pairs from a real-world learning platform, followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to improve long-horizon planning. In deployment, the framework includes learner profiling from interaction traces, retrieval of candidate learning actions, policy-based path planning, and adaptive delivery that generates personalized narrative bridges and instructional content.

The empirical context includes data from a real-world learning platform with 300 learning sessions and 14,584 interaction turns, plus a real-world user study with 22 undergraduate students. In the user study, participants were randomly assigned to either the full Pxplore system or a retrieval-based baseline. All participants completed an introductory lesson, then proceeded to a next lesson chosen either by Pxplore or the baseline system, followed by tests and learner-experience surveys. The work appears to be situated at Tsinghua University in China, and the deployed system is an online learning platform.

The main conclusions are that Pxplore outperforms prompt-only LLM baselines, inference-guided LLMs, supervised fine-tuned baselines, and retrieval-only approaches on pedagogical alignment and action-ranking quality. In the real-world study, the Pxplore group showed larger pre/post knowledge gains and higher ratings for relevance, personalization, motivation, and satisfaction than the control group. The authors conclude that structured learner state modeling plus reinforcement learning can support more coherent, goal-driven, and personalized learning paths, though the user study is small and short-term.

identified_tools.name: Pxplore
identified_tools.description: An LLM-driven personalized learning path planning framework that models learner state, uses reinforcement learning (SFT + GRPO) to select next learning actions, and supports adaptive instructional delivery.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a deployed personalized learning path planning system that profiles learners, plans goal-aligned next lessons/actions, and adaptively delivers content within an online learning platform.

findings.finding_summary: In a controlled real-world user study, students using Pxplore showed larger pre/post knowledge gains than a retrieval-based baseline. Mean test scores increased from 61.81% pre-test to 90.09% post-test for the Pxplore group, a reported knowledge gain of +28.28%; the paper states this was greater than the control group's improvement, although the control group's exact scores were not numerically reported in text.
findings.measure: Pre-test and post-test learning assessment scores (multiple-choice and short-answer questions)

findings.finding_summary: Pxplore improved subjective learner experience relative to the retrieval-based baseline, with especially strong gains in Motivation and Satisfaction. The paper reports Motivation = 4.73 and Satisfaction = 4.64 for Pxplore, with additional reported advantages in Relevance (+0.36) and Personalization (+0.18) on 5-point Likert scales.
findings.measure: Learner experience survey ratings on 5-point Likert scales: Helpfulness, Diversity, Relevance, Personalization, Clarity, Motivation, Understanding, Satisfaction

findings.finding_summary: In offline evaluation of the planning policy, Pxplore achieved the best pedagogical alignment among compared systems. The GRPO-trained Qwen-based Pxplore reached an overall alignment rate of 65.47%, compared with 62.68% for the SFT Qwen model and 58.48% for GPT-4o with inference-time guidance; total reward was 182.0.
findings.measure: Average pedagogical alignment rate and reward computation R(·) in offline planning evaluation
findings.sample_size: test split derived from 300 sessions; exact evaluation n not separately reported

findings.finding_summary: Pxplore's profiling module outperformed a GPT-4o baseline in blind evaluation by human annotators and LLM judges. Reported improvements were largest in Interpretability and Explainability (+17.7%), followed by Interest Identification Accuracy (+6.26%) and Actionability and Utility (+6.63%), for an overall increase of +7.88%; human annotator agreement exceeded Pearson r > 0.8.
findings.measure: Profile quality ratings across Interest Identification Accuracy, Profile Completeness, Actionability and Utility, and Interpretability and Explainability
findings.effect_size: overall +7.88%; IE +17.7%; IIA +6.26%; AU +6.63%; Pearson r>0.8
findings.sample_size: derived from curated dataset of 300 learning sessions; exact number of rated profiles not reported

findings.finding_summary: For adaptive delivery, Pxplore's generated instructional content was rated higher than original materials across pedagogical dimensions. The largest gains were in Motivational Appeal (+17.2%), Personalization & Empathy (+14.9%), and Pedagogical Scaffolding (+12.4%), with an overall improvement of +10.7%; Conciseness & Efficiency improved only marginally (+3.1%).
findings.measure: Blind human and LLM-judge ratings of delivery quality across Contextual Coherence, Personalization & Empathy, Pedagogical Scaffolding, Conciseness & Efficiency, and Motivational Appeal
findings.sample_size: exact number of rated items not_reported

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language models used here as baseline evaluators/generators rather than the core intervention.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as baseline prompt-based and inference-guided planning models (via GPT-4o / 4o-mini), as a profile-generation baseline, and to help construct metadata and learner-state representations.

findings.finding_summary: As a planning baseline, ChatGPT-family models underperformed Pxplore on pedagogical alignment. GPT-4o achieved 52.52% average alignment and total reward 145.8 in prompt-based form, improving to 58.48% and reward 169.0 with inference-time learner-state guidance, but remaining below Pxplore's best result of 65.47%.
findings.measure: Average pedagogical alignment rate and reward computation R(·) in offline planning evaluation
findings.sample_size: test split derived from 300 sessions; exact evaluation n not separately reported

identified_tools.name: Qwen
identified_tools.description: Alibaba Qwen-family large language model used as the base model family within the Pxplore training pipeline and as a standalone baseline.
identified_tools.use_case: Used both as a baseline LLM and as the underlying base model for SFT and GRPO-trained Pxplore variants in offline planning evaluation.

findings.finding_summary: Qwen performance improved substantially when incorporated into the Pxplore training pipeline. Standalone Qwen3 achieved 39.73% average alignment and reward 116.0; Qwen SFT reached 62.68% and reward 178.0; Pxplore_Qwen3 achieved the best reported result at 65.47% alignment and reward 182.0.
findings.measure: Average pedagogical alignment rate and reward computation R(·) in offline planning evaluation
findings.sample_size: test split derived from 300 sessions; exact evaluation n not separately reported

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: Meta LLaMA-family large language model used as a baseline model family and as the base model for a Pxplore-trained variant.
identified_tools.use_case: Used both as a baseline LLM and as the underlying base model for SFT and GRPO-trained Pxplore variants in offline planning evaluation.

findings.finding_summary: LLaMA performance also improved within the Pxplore training paradigm. Standalone Llama3.1 achieved 43.17% average alignment and reward 120.0; Llama3.1 SFT reached 60.00% and reward 171.0; Pxplore_Llama3.1 achieved 63.48% alignment and reward 179.0.
findings.measure: Average pedagogical alignment rate and reward computation R(·) in offline planning evaluation
findings.sample_size: test split derived from 300 sessions; exact evaluation n not separately reported

quality_tier_rationale: The paper includes empirical evaluations and a small controlled user study with random assignment, but the real-world sample is very small (N=22) and many reported outcomes are offline alignment metrics or human/LLM ratings rather than standardized educational measures. Effect estimates and uncertainty statistics are limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects are consistently positive, including a sizeable within-group test score gain (+28.28%) and improved learner experience, but the absence of standardized effect sizes and limited sample/reporting make the overall practical impact modest-to-promising rather than definitively large.
